subject: QuantumLane private deploy - connection path evaluation
messages:
From: Maria Alvarez <maria@quantumlane.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Connection path for QuantumLane private deploy

Aditya — thanks for taking this on. Were nearing our infra cutover window and need guidance choosing a primary connectivity pattern between our on-prem datacenter (Chicago colo) and the AWS VPC that will host the Redwood Private nodes. Our key constraints: low and consistent RTT for inference traffic (goal: steady p50 <10ms), strict egress control (SOCs, IP allowlists), strong auditability for flows, and the ability to failover without app changes.

Current environment summary attached (quantumlane-network-inventory.pdf). Quick facts:
- On-prem -> internet egress via dedicated transit; AWS account is separate from our main infra account (cross-account).
- Avg QPS to model endpoints: 1.2k r/s, burst up to 5k r/s during processing windows.
- Data classification: regulated PII in prompts; we must avoid exposure to public internet.

Options were considering: VPC Peering (cross-account peering), AWS PrivateLink (Interface Endpoint to Redwood service), Site-to-Site VPN (IPsec) from colo to VPC. Please provide a recommendation that balances latency, operational risk, and audit/compliance requirements — and call out whether a dual-path strategy (primary + fallback) makes sense. Also list any network changes we should prepare for.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call.

--
Maria Alvarez
Head of Infrastructure, QuantumLane
attachments: quantumlane-network-inventory.pdf, quantumlane-soc2-questions.xlsx

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Alvarez <maria@quantumlane.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-18T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Connection path for QuantumLane private deploy

Maria — thanks for the inventory and the clear constraints. Looping in Kim (solutions) and Connor (security) to produce a recommendation and an ops checklist. High-level quick take to get the ball rolling: 

- PrivateLink (interface endpoint) gives the best attack surface control: service scoped to your ENIs, no cross-account route-table fiddling, and traffic stays inside AWS fabric. Latency typically slightly higher than peering but more predictable in cross-account scenarios.
- VPC Peering can deliver lowest single-digit ms RTT inside a region but is non-transitive and requires route/bgp work for cross-account; also exposes your VPC CIDR to Redwood which may be undesirable for compliance.
- Site-to-site VPN (IPsec) is the most familiar for colo folks and gives clear perimeter boundaries. It can be fine for baseline traffic but adds more variable latency and throughput limits unless you use multiple tunnels or a managed transit gateway with BGP.

Connor/Kim: can you sketch an opinionated recommended path (one primary, one fallback) and a minimal test plan? Also note any ACL/KMS/observability hooks we should ask QuantumLane to prep.

I'll set up a 45min sync with QuantumLane tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks,
--
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-privatelink-setup-checklist.md

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Maria Alvarez <maria@quantumlane.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Tim Chan <tim.chan@quantumlane.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T08:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Connection path for QuantumLane private deploy

Thanks — I sketched a recommendation and an ops playbook below. Long story short: recommend PrivateLink as primary with an IPsec S2S VPN as resilient fallback. Rationale and action items follow.

Executive recommendation (primary + fallback):
- Primary: AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoint) from QuantumLane VPC(s) to Redwood Private service. Reasons: minimal network exposure (no VPC route disclosure), per-endpoint security groups for allowlisting, easier cross-account access model, and strong compatibility with cross-account managed services. It aligns best with SOC2-style controls because you can limit Egress to a specific endpoint and keep monitoring tied to ENI flows.
- Fallback: Site-to-Site IPsec VPN (two tunnels, BGP-enabled) terminating into a dedicated Transit Gateway or a small NAT/HA pair in the QuantumLane VPC. Use VPN for DR and for on-prem app traffic that must not change routing on failover.

Detailed trade-offs:
- Latency: Peering <= PrivateLink < S2S VPN (generally). If you need sub-5ms consistently, VPC peering is the likely winner but only if both VPCs are in the same AZ footprint and you accept CIDR exposure. PrivateLink overhead is small (single-digit ms) but more consistent for cross-account services. VPN adds NAT/IPsec overhead and variable latency.
- Throughput & scaling: PrivateLink supports ENI-backed throughput and scales with endpoint ENIs; for sustained 5k r/s with large payloads plan endpoint capacity and use NLB-backed service endpoints. For VPN, expect aggregate throughput limits per tunnel (consider multiple tunnels and ECMP). Peering scales naturally but requires careful route management across accounts/regions.
- Security & compliance: PrivateLink is easiest to explain to auditors (service endpoint + SGs + flow logs). Peering requires sharing route tables and CIDRs which complicates least-privilege design. VPN shows clear egress points and can be instrumented for packet capture in colo for audits.
- Operational complexity: PrivateLink simplifies cross-account onboarding but requires endpoint provisioning and security group design. Peering requires bilateral acceptance and no transitive routes (so multi-VPC topologies get complex). VPN needs strong monitoring and keepalive config; certificate/key rotation must be operationalized.

Suggested architecture pattern (practical):
1) Create a PrivateLink service in Redwood's hosting account; QuantumLane creates interface endpoints in their VPC(s). Use security groups to only permit IPs/subnets for your application subnets.
2) Configure endpoint ENI flow logs (to CloudWatch/your SIEM) and enable VPC Flow Logs for the VPC subnet carrying the interface endpoint.
3) Provision an IPsec S2S VPN (two tunnels) between QuantumLane colo edge and a Transit Gateway or an HA NAT pair in the VPC. Advertise routes via BGP for automated failover.
4) Implement a simple routing policy: VPC route table prefers PrivateLink for Redwood service prefix; a short BGP route-preference policy causes VPN to take precedence only if PrivateLink health checks fail (we can coordinate health probes via our control plane).

Test plan (minimal):
- Phase 1 (Lab): Create PrivateLink endpoint in a staging VPC. Validate TLS, SG allowlist, and that metrics (latency, error-rate) are within SLA.
- Phase 2 (Load): Ramp to 150% of expected peak (7.5k r/s) for 1 hour; verify CPU/GPU headroom and endpoint throughput.
- Phase 3 (Failover): Simulate PrivateLink service endpoint failure (or block SG) and validate automatic traffic failover to VPN path, verify session recovery and error budgets.

Ops checklist / pre-reqs for QuantumLane:
- Provide a conservative CIDR range(s) intended for service subnets; avoid overlapping with Redwood VPC CIDRs.
- Network ACLs and SG rules for interface endpoints: list the minimal allowed ports (TLS 443) and management CIDRs.
- Run IP inventory and share device NAT/edge capabilities so we can size VPN tunnels (ipsec-config-sample.txt attached).
- Audit requirements: enable VPC Flow Logs and share access path to logs (s3 path or SIEM ingestion).

Attachments we recommend we exchange now: redwood-privatelink-setup-checklist.md (Ive attached a slim checklist), ipsec-config-sample.txt, plus your inventory. Ill open a stub runbook in your HubSpot (link below) and add the test-plan tasks.

If QuantumLane needs sub-5ms p50 across regions / multiple AZs we can revisit peering for limited VPCs, but that will require tighter IP governance and additional network justification for auditors.

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-privatelink-setup-checklist.md, ipsec-config-sample.txt

- Provision the endpoint subnets and share the CIDR ranges by EOD tomorrow.
- Turn on VPC Flow Logs to an s3 bucket and share the ARN (QL-logs-prod).
- Run a quick throughput test on our colo edge and share results (should be able to sustain multiple 1Gbps flows).

Lets keep the sync tomorrow at 10am CT; Tim and I will bring the network folks so we can agree on the Canaries and the BGP preference. Ive attached the SOC2 questionnaire items that are still open (quantumlane-soc2-questions.xlsx).
